title: PostgreSQL Fixes 12-Year-Old Logical Decoding Flaw Enabling Replication-Role Code Execution
blurb: A bug that sat undetected in PostgreSQL's replication internals for 12 years let a replication-role account execute arbitrary code -- a reminder that trusted internal roles need the same scrutiny as external attack surface.

title: New Ted Backdoor Hides Inside Victims' Own HAProxy Builds to Intercept Web Traffic
blurb: Malware that patches itself into a victim's own compiled HAProxy binary blurs the line between "infected" and "normal" infrastructure, making traffic-interception backdoors far harder to spot.

title: "Top-down Zelda meets Bloodborne": action RPG Withering Realms is out now in early access, should you fancy riding the shoulders of a horrible doll
blurb: A notable indie early-access launch mixing top-down Zelda structure with Bloodborne-style combat and body horror.

title: I've found DLSS 5 can slash frame rates by up to 73% on an RTX 5080 gaming PC in NBA 2K27, and I'm wondering what kind of mega-rig would justify the performance hit
blurb: A concrete, measured regression showing Nvidia's newest neural-rendering feature can cost more performance than it saves on current high-end hardware.

title: Second complete map of a fruit fly brain completed
blurb: A second full connectome -- every neuron and synapse mapped -- gives researchers their first same-species comparison of brain wiring between sexes.

title: Magic-angle graphene provides evidence for unconventional superconductivity
blurb: New experimental evidence strengthens the case that twisted-bilayer graphene hosts a genuinely unconventional (non-BCS) superconducting mechanism, a long-sought condensed-matter result.

title: Reversing MikroTik's Silent Patch: The RouterOS 7.23.4 Fix They Wouldn't Explain
blurb: Independent reverse engineering of an undisclosed RouterOS patch, filling in details the vendor left out of its changelog.

title: Show HN: Open-Source eInk Bike Computer
blurb: A fully open-source, low-power eInk bike computer -- hardware, firmware, and design files all published for others to build.

title: New CrowdStrike 'FalconFlank' zero-day grants SYSTEM privileges
blurb: Problem: CrowdStrike's Falcon endpoint-security agent -- meant to stop attackers -- has an unpatched Windows privilege-escalation bug. Approach: researcher "Nightmare Eclipse" found that Falcon's macro-remediation feature (auto-removes malicious Office macros) can be tricked into running attacker code with Falcon's own elevated permissions. Result: on fully updated Windows 11 / Server 2025, the exploit pops a SYSTEM command prompt. No CVE yet; CrowdStrike is investigating and offers only a workaround. The same researcher dropped similar zero-days this week against Kaspersky, Avast, and Nvidia. Why it matters: the tool trusted to catch privilege escalation is itself the escalation path, across several security vendors at once. Glossary: EDR (endpoint detection & response agent); SYSTEM (Windows' highest privilege level); 0day (unpatched, disclosed vulnerability); PoC (proof-of-concept exploit code).

title: Making a Pole Balance Itself With Propellers
blurb: Problem: balancing a pole on a fingertip is a classic trick; no hands makes it harder. Approach: builder Peter Ryseck mounted a small drone (flight controller, battery, three propellers) atop a free-standing pole, using thrust to keep it upright like a self-stabilizing quadcopter. Result: chasing perfect vertical balance caused wild oscillation, so Ryseck let the pole lean into the wind instead, a more stable configuration. Switching from 10-inch to 5-inch propellers cut inertia enough to react fast enough to stay up. Why it matters: drone stabilization generalizes to non-flying balance problems, and "more stable" needn't mean "more upright." Glossary: flight controller (board running the stabilization algorithm); active stabilization (continuously correcting orientation); inertia (resistance to rotation change); oscillation (unstable overcorrection loop).
